data.body:
What you get

  • Two short files you set up once: how you write, and who you are. Both shown filled in for an example person.
  • Ten ready requests for what you send most.
  • A quick check before you hit send.

The ten

  • An email to a client
  • An email to a supplier
  • An update to your team or board
  • A complaint to a company
  • A request to a landlord or service provider
  • Saying no politely
  • A thank-you message
  • A reference for someone
  • A follow-up when nobody replied
  • A reply to a tricky message

Each one ends with the same two lines: "Use only the facts I've given you. If something you need is missing, ask me before you write."

Three of the ten, first lines

An email to a client. Something changed: a delay, a price, a date.

What happened: [the change].

Why: [the reason, in a sentence].

What happens next: [the new date, price or step].

See it in fullClose

When: something changed for a client, such as a delay, a price or a date.

Using my voice file and my About Me file, write a short email to [name], a client who [one line about them].

What happened: [the change].

Why: [the reason, in a sentence].

What happens next: [the new date, price or step].

What I need from them: [nothing / a reply by a date / a decision].

Under [150] words. Lead with the news. Don't apologize more than once.

Use only the facts I've given you. If something you need is missing, ask me before you write.

Good answer: the news in the first two sentences, the reason in one, the next step last.

Check: is every date and amount yours? Did it promise something you didn't, like "no extra cost"?

An email to a supplier. Orders are late or wrong, and you want it fixed without burning the relationship.

The problem: [what went wrong, with numbers].

The orders: [order or PO numbers, due dates and arrival dates].

What it cost us: [one line].

See it in fullClose

When: orders are late or wrong, and you want it fixed without burning the relationship.

Using my voice file and my About Me file, write an email to [name] at [supplier].

The problem: [what went wrong, with numbers].

The orders: [order or PO numbers, due dates and arrival dates].

What it cost us: [one line].

What I want: [a call this week / a written plan by a date / a credit].

We want to keep working with them. Firm, not angry. Under [150] words.

Use only the facts I've given you. If something you need is missing, ask me before you write.

Good answer: your numbers, what it cost, one clear ask with a date.

Check: are the numbers unchanged? Did it threaten anything you won't do?

A reply to a tricky message. Someone sent something awkward or pushy, and you want to answer well.

Their message: [paste it, with account numbers and other people's details covered].

What I want to say: [your answer in one or two plain lines].

What I won't do: [anything you won't agree to].

See it in fullClose

When: someone sent you something awkward, upset or pushy, and you want to answer well without getting pulled in.

Using my voice file and my About Me file, write a reply to the message below from [name], who is my [client / colleague / neighbour / family member].

Their message: [paste it, with account numbers and other people's details covered].

What I want to say: [your answer in one or two plain lines].

What I won't do: [anything you won't agree to].

Calm and short. Answer what they asked, and don't argue every point. Under [150] words.

Use only the facts I've given you. If something you need is missing, ask me before you write.

Good answer: calm, answers the real question, says your position once, no new promises.

Check: read it as them. Would it calm things down or start round two? Did it agree to anything you listed under "won't do"?

What it is

A 20-page PDF guide written for ChatGPT, for your own use. Instant download plus an email. A 30-day money-back guarantee covers this purchase: email elvin@elvinpeters.com within 30 days for a full refund, and you keep the files.
